findings.note: templates/mutation-incremental/lib/run.mjs:64 reads process.env.MUTATION_TEST_DISABLE_RESIDUAL unconditionally in the production executeIncremental path (passed as disableResidual to computePlan). It is an undocumented (outside the e2e README) hidden switch that can silently disable residual re-verification for any invocation, not just the e2e harness. Low risk because it requires deliberately setting an unusual env var and is explained/used only by testdata/mutation-incremental-e2e/README.md's negative-control scenario (lines 100-105), but a stray env var of that name in a real CI environment would silently change verdict semantics with no warning.

templates/mutation-incremental/lib/run.mjs previously threw a UsageError when --pr was combined with pendingOnPr: 'allow' (deleted line: 'if (options.pr && config.pendingOnPr === "allow") throw new UsageError(...)'). The replacement comment above the new `routed` computation (run.mjs line ~164) documents the new behavior (a PR run under 'allow' becomes an ordinary, unrouted run) but this is a user-visible CLI behavior change — a previously-rejected invocation now silently succeeds with different semantics (maxMinutes dropped). Worth confirming docs/mutation-harness.md documents this so operators relying on the old validation error aren't surprised. Not blocking: the change is intentional and spec-referenced (§11.2) and covered indirectly by routeFor's exhaustive test table in deferrals.test.mjs.
